transcript.text: Samsung WD90T534DBW washer dryer - clothes are still damp at the end of the wash and dry programme. It's not that old. Is the heater going?

To answer your question directly: it is unlikely to be the heater first. The most common cause of damp clothes in a washer-dryer is restricted airflow, not a failed part. Before we look at internal components, could you please check the pump filter (usually behind a small flap at the bottom front)? Please unplug the machine, place towels down, and see if it's full of fluff or debris.
I haven't checked the pump filter, so I can't tell you what's in it. Is there anything else I should look at? The drum does get hot during drying, if that helps.

The fact that the drum gets hot is very useful—it means your heating element is likely working correctly. Since it's getting hot but clothes are still damp, the issue is almost certainly restricted airflow or condensation. On Samsung washer-dryers like yours, this is most often caused by a blocked condenser (the component that cools steam back into water) or a clogged lint filter. If these are full of fluff, moisture can't escape and clothes come out wet. Could you please unplug the machine and check if there is a removable condenser unit? It's often located behind the bottom right panel or inside the pump filter housing. If you find one, it usually needs rinsing under a tap to clear out fluff and lint.

I'm not sure there's a removable condenser on this model, I haven't seen one. Do you want me to check anything about how I'm loading it instead? I usually do a full drum on Wash+Dry with Cupboard Dry.

Yes, that is almost certainly your problem. If you put a full drum straight onto a drying programme, the moisture cannot circulate properly and the clothes will come out damp. To fix this, split your load in half when using the drying function. For example, if you have washed 8kg of laundry, dry only about 4–5kg at a time. This simple change usually resolves the issue completely without needing any repairs.
